directAnswer: You can check your CPU model by using system information tools available in your operating system, such as Task Manager on Windows or System Information on macOS.
summary: This guide provides steps to check your CPU model across different platforms, along with some common questions and considerations.

sections.heading: Checking CPU Model on Windows
sections.body: On Windows, you can use Task Manager or Command Prompt to find your CPU model. Task Manager provides a user-friendly interface, while Command Prompt offers a quick text-based method.

sections.heading: Checking CPU Model on macOS
sections.body: On macOS, the System Information tool provides detailed information about your hardware, including the CPU model. You can access it easily from the Apple menu.

sections.heading: Checking CPU Model on Linux
sections.body: On Linux, you can use the terminal command 'lscpu' or check the contents of '/proc/cpuinfo' to find detailed information about your CPU.

steps.title: Using Task Manager on Windows
steps.detail: Right-click the taskbar and select 'Task Manager'. Click on the 'Performance' tab, then select 'CPU' to view the model information.

steps.title: Using Command Prompt on Windows
steps.detail: Open Command Prompt and type 'wmic cpu get name'. Press Enter to see your CPU model.

steps.title: Using System Information on macOS
steps.detail: Click the Apple logo in the top-left corner, select 'About This Mac', and then click 'System Report'. Under 'Hardware', you will find your CPU model.

steps.title: Using Terminal on Linux
steps.detail: Open a terminal and type 'lscpu' or 'cat /proc/cpuinfo' and press Enter to display your CPU model.

faqs.question: Can I check my CPU model without any software?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can check your CPU model through the BIOS/UEFI settings during system boot, but this method requires restarting your computer.

faqs.question: What if my CPU model is not displayed correctly?
faqs.answer: If your CPU model is not displayed correctly, ensure that your system drivers are up to date and check for any hardware issues.

faqs.question: Is there a difference between CPU model and CPU architecture?
faqs.answer: Yes, the CPU model refers to the specific version of the processor, while CPU architecture refers to the design and instruction set used by that model.

caveats: Steps may vary slightly depending on the version of the operating system.
